title: Simplify editor game speed implementation - PROOF OF CONCEPT

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Reverts the implementation of #107273 and allows adjusting game speed by a simple wall clock multiplier.

Fixes #122242.
Fixes #122217.

Simpler (non-UI) implementation for https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12555.

It is possible (at least in theory) to modify game speed and make no other modifications to the engine simply by changing how the wall clock progresses.

I wasn't party to the original proposal / implementation so have no idea why it was chosen to go that way. It seems (to my eyes, unless I am missing something) overly complicated and bug-prone, for something that can likely be kept very simple. The current implementation also seems to be passing complexity on to users, hence the above issues.

There might be some systems (e.g. profiling, network etc) that work better accessing raw ticks rather than this scaled timing (in which case they can call the `get_raw_ticks_usec()` version), but essentially just using a scaled version should *just work* :tm: in most circumstances I suspect.

_An obvious alternative is to have `get_ticks_usec()` return raw ticks, and another function like `get_scaled_ticks_usec()` only for the time scaled version. It depends which would cause the greater churn._

## Proof of concept
This is very much a simple proof of concept, it compiles and runs and seems to work fine.

For final production there are a couple more considerations:
* backward compatibility - we might need stubs for APIs put in during #107273 which are now redundant
* lockless - it's possible to make the main `get_ticks_usec()` lockless with atomics. However I've kept the code here simple with a mutex so it's easy to understand.

## Notes
* Draft as this is more for discussion.
* Most of this is reverting #107273, the actual changes for the feature are only a few lines.
* Works using a multiplier for each call (i.e. each individual delta resyncs the wall clock). This prevents overflow bugs, but could lead theoretically lead to some sampling error in the case of low frequency clocks and rapid calls to `get_ticks_usec()`, but this is mostly for game debugging as I understand it, and unlikely to be a problem in practice.
* It's also possible to just have a sync point when setting scale as a one off, but then you have to deal properly with overflow (e.g. using 128 bit fixed point), especially when lockless, so left that for refinement if we decide to go ahead with this approach.

## Extra
Something else I noticed is that Godot is missing a frame cached time. We do pass a `delta` to `_process()`, which is effectively a frame cached time, but there's potentially a bunch of other calls in the engine which only need to know the time at the start of a frame, rather than the exact wall clock time (which will be subject to random effects, and also be more expensive to read).
